title: Gibberish after all? Voynichese is statistically similar to human-produced samples of meaningless text
authors: Daniel E. Gaskell and Claire L. Bowern
summary: The authors compare short handwritten pseudotexts from 42 volunteers with several Voynich transliterations and a broader corpus of meaningful text. This makes structured human pseudotext available as a comparison for manuscript statistics.
established: Across samples, the human pseudotexts covered Voynich-like values for almost all tested low-level measures, including some commonly used as indicators of natural language.
The main uncovered Voynich feature was the magnitude of glyph-position bias within words. The volunteers wrote in lowercase Latin characters, limiting tests of position-specific visual forms.
The classifier trained on these data put most Voynich renderings closer to the human pseudotext samples. The authors limit the inference to the corpus and features studied.

open.question: Can human-produced pseudotext over a longer writing session reproduce manuscript-scale clustering of vocabulary across pages and sections?
open.check: Collect independent long samples or test a frozen model motivated by the documented volunteer strategies. Match lengths and layout and compare local clustering and cross-section drift jointly.
